Sunday rant.\n\n21.6 billion ADA staked. That's roughly 60% of circulating supply sitting in stake pools earning yield while remaining fully liquid. No lockups, no slashing risk, no minimum delegation. Just park it and earn.\n\nCompare that to Ethereum where you either lock 32 ETH in a validator, hand your keys to Lido, or accept whatever wrapped derivative they're selling this week. Solana slashes you if your validator misbehaves. Cardano? Delegate to a different pool next epoch if yours underperforms. Zero friction.\n\nThe 5000 pool count tells you something too. That's not a typo. Five thousand independent stake pools competing for delegation. Try running a validator on most chains and you'll need enterprise hardware and a small fortune in locked capital. Here you can spin up a pool on modest specs and the protocol handles the rest.\n\nMeanwhile 1.5 billion ADA sitting in treasury waiting for community governance to allocate it. No VC unlock schedule. No foundation deciding behind closed doors. Just on-chain voting when the infrastructure matures.\n\n84k transactions in an epoch isn't going to win any TPS wars but it's real usage, not wash trading to juice metrics for the next funding round. YMMV on what counts as adoption but I'll take organic over inflated every time.\n\nThe narrative says ghost chain. Wyoming And Spokane Data Center Pauses Show NIMBY Fury Has Shifted From Nuclear To AI\n\nWyoming And Spokane Data Center Pauses Show NIMBY Fury Has Shifted From Nuclear To AI\n\n            \n\nThe latest cracks in the data center buildout story arrived this month from opposite ends of the energy-rich West. Crusoe paused development activities on its 1.8 GW “Project Jade” campus near Cheyenne, Wyoming, at the explicit request of its customer. \n\nJust days later, Avista announced it was pausing processing of a 500 MW data center request in Spokane County after more than 5,000 community complaints, a proposed city council moratorium, and concerns over ratepayer costs and legacy contamination at the former Kaiser Aluminum smelter site.\n\nThis all fits the pattern we’ve documented for over a year with proposed US data center capacity colliding with local political reality, transmission bottlenecks, and raw NIMBY resistance that now appears more intense than the peak opposition nuclear power plants faced in prior decades.\n\n71% of Americans https://news.gallup.com/poll/709772/americans-oppose-data-centers-area.aspx construction of an AI data center in their local area, with 48% strongly opposed. \n\nhttps://cms.zerohedge.com/s3/files/inline-images/Seven-in-10-Americans-Oppose-Local-Construction-of-AI-Data-Centers.png?itok=-kBOAeUe\n\nBy comparison, https://news.gallup.com/poll/708620/less-support-solar-wind-energy-nuclear.aspx to a nuclear plant in the same backyard stands at 53%. \n\nhttps://cms.zerohedge.com/s3/files/inline-images/Americans-Support-for-Local-Nuclear-Energy-Plant-.png?itok=4bhbTtph\n\nData centers have managed to poll worse on local acceptance than nuclear facilities ever did at the height of their controversy. \n\nWe have been pounding the table on this long enough that we're frankly surprised the table is still standing. Half of the US data center capacity originally slated to begin operations in 2026 faces delays or outright cancellation, according to Sightline Climate analysis we https://www.zerohedge.com/technology/half-us-data-centers-are-set-be-canceled-or-delayed-2026 in April.\n\nContested projects are seeing roughly 40% cancellation rates in some analyses. Eminent domain https://www.zerohedge.com/energy/homeowners-face-eminent-domain-bulldozers-ai-data-centers-demand-new-power over transmission lines have erupted in Maryland, Georgia, and elsewhere. Brookfield-backed Compass withdrew from a major Northern Virginia corridor. Community https://www.zerohedge.com/energy/americas-growing-pushback-against-data-centers have already killed or delayed billions in projects from Texas to the Midwest. \n\nThe Avista and Crusoe cases simply add fresh, high-profile confirmation that even brownfield sites with existing power infrastructure and willing utilities are not immune.\n\nThe investment implications for the nuclear sector are direct and near-term negative for sentiment, even if the long-term logic remains intact. The explosive AI-driven power demand narrative that helped lift names such as Oklo (OKLO), NuScale (SMR), NANO Nuclear (NNE), Cameco (CCJ), and the broader sector via URA, NLR, and NUKZ, has always rested on the assumption that hyperscale load growth would translate into contracted, financeable nuclear capacity on accelerated timelines. \n\nWhen marquee data center campuses pause or reconfigure, that assumption gets stress-tested. Equity volatility in the nuclear complex has reflected exactly this uncertainty with profit-taking and narrative recalibration whenever friction in the demand side becomes visible.\n\nNone of this changes the structural math. The US still adds essentially zero new large reactors while China commissions multiple units per year. AI training and inference loads are real and growing. But the notion that private capital and hyperscaler demand alone would bulldoze through local opposition and grid constraints was always optimistic. \n\nThese latest pauses demonstrate that the problem is not unique to nuclear permitting. It is a systemic feature of American infrastructure development in the current political and regulatory environment.\n\n      https://cms.zerohedge.com/users/tyler-durden\nTue, 06/16/2026 - 18:00\n\nhttps://www.zerohedge.com/technology/wyoming-and-spokane-data-center-pauses-show-nimby-fury-has-shifted-nuclear-ai

[1037] 06-16 18:42 f4d61c10ce96cdac39d1240133050034980c2a221331653d13f0a404d73917e5 d0ed1eb980bb9d178771f52df71dfcf38264d431d2c1bb3df14b278532cbb8ba
I started the Kincaid DNA project in June 2002.  It was one of the first surname projects at Family Tree DNA.  My first batch of kits started with 1255.  #Dna testing gave us Kincaid's a real surprise in that the early Kincaid's did not have clan / celtic signature.  We were Germanic in origin.\n\nThis set off a lot of backlash against me from American Highland Game enthusiasts who were adamant we were indeed Gaelic.  As one who likes to follow evidence and truth I parted ways with the American Clan Kincaid Society  and in 2010 I set up a new #Kincaid web site / group  exploring our true origins.  The group did not last, but the web site continued up till recently.  I took it offline last month as several research documents were removed without my knowledge and I wanted to prevent AI bots from harvesting my research without crediting me.  I will be integrating things with nostr going forward.\n\nThe following was the launch of kyncades.org.\n\nPeter\n\n===============================\n\nReturn-Path: <kincaid-bounces@rootsweb.com>\nReceived: from torspm01.toronto.rmgopenwave.com ([66.43.27.40])\n          by tormta05.toronto.rmgopenwave.com\n          (InterMail vM.8.00.01.00 201-2244-105-20090324) with ESMTP\n          id <20100722215103.IXCL19509.tormta05.toronto.rmgopenwave.com@torspm01.toronto.rmgopenwave.com>\n          for <7kincaid@nb.sympatico.ca>; Us Kincaid's were fortunate to have a real Internet pioneer in Grant Kinkead of Melbourne, Australia.  His company Alphalink was part of the second wave of startups there.  He was kind enough to host my initial web site for free as well as my later kyncades.org site and a new Clan Kincaid web site and the Kincaid DNA project.  Grant also gave valuable help with the look of the first Clan Kincaid web pages.\n\nThere was a real problem with others stealing research (much like AI bots today) from the beginning. #norgstr  bitmynt stenger. Fra nettsiden til bitmynt: «Bitmynt stengjer ned vekslingstenesta\n\nDå eg starta opp mi enkle vekslingsteneste i 2010, var det nesten umogeleg å veksle mellom BTC og NOK. Tenester som MtGox eksisterte, men mangla bankkonto og var difor nesten umogeleg å handle på. Elles var ein avhengig av å finne nokon på Bitcointalk eller IRC. Ingen andre norske veksla.\n\nEg byrja å tilby veksling på IRC-kanalen #bitcoin-otc. Der er eg framleis den einaste med over 1000 i samla rating: https://bitcoin-otc.com/viewratings.php\n\nHausten 2013 tente eg mykje meir på robothandel enn på min vanlege jobb, og omsetnaden hadde teke seg opp kraftig. Då sa eg opp jobben for å starte Bitmynt AS og for å drive med bitcoinhandel på fulltid.\n\nDerifrå starta ein lang kamp mot bankane. Eg vil ikkje gå i detaljar om den her. Det vert ein annan gong.\n\nFrå og med den 15. oktober 2018 kom Bitcoin under kvitvaskingslova. Eg dreiv framleis handelen som privatperson, men måtte forhalde meg til den. Finanstilsynet kom med på laget, og eg fekk endeleg bankkonto. I 2019, etter 6 års kamp mot bankar og med haugevis av stengde bankkonti, oppsagde kundeforhold og ei rettssak mot Nordea bak meg, kunne eg endeleg starte Bitmynt AS og tilsetje folk!\n\nMålet var å starte ei teneste som kunne gjere bitcoin-brukarar uavhengige av norsk bankkonto, men utan å oppbevare bitcoin for kundar. Vi skulle tilby veksling, rekningsbetaling, lønsutbetaling for bedrifter og måtar tredjepartar kunne sende oss NOK for veksling til BTC som kunden vår kunne motta til si private lommebok med sine private nøklar. Alt dette var mogeleg innanfor kvitvaskingslova frå 2018. Sovidt eg kan sjå, er det framleis mogeleg etter MiCA, men veldig mykje vanskelegare.\n\nVi kom ikkje i mål. Det er mange grunnar til dette. Ein vesentleg grunn var at eg sjølv hadde fått blodkreft og fekk stadig mindre energi, og trudde sjølv at eg var utbrend. Kreften vart diagnostisert i desember 2020. No er kreften gradvis på veg ut av kroppen, for det finst heldigvis god medisin, men medisinen har òg biverknader. Kreften kom på verst mogelege tidspunkt.\n\nFrå 1. juli vert MiCA innført i Noreg. Den set veldig mykje strengare krav til vekslingstenester. Det er i praksis ikkje lenger mogeleg å drive ei enkelt vekslingsteneste, frå no av er regelverket like strengt som for finansinstitusjonar.\n\nMitt ynskje var aldri å verte nokon form for bank. Eg skulle drive ei enkel vekslingsteneste.\n\nDei siste åra har vi heldigvis fått fleire konkurrentar. Det har vore viktig for meg, for no er vi ikkje lenger eitt svakt punkt som bankane kan gå til åtak på for å i praksis forby bitcoin i Noreg. Eg har støtta fleire av dei med likviditet og investeringar. Difor er det heilt greitt å setje punktum no. Det vil framleis vere mogeleg å veksle mellom bitcoin og norske kroner i Noreg utan meg. Vi har difor valt å ikkje søkje om konsesjon etter MiCA, med alle formalitetane som må på plass og alt byråkratiet og jussen rundt.\n\nDen 16. juni 2026 er det difor slutt. Då har vi eit par veker til å rydde opp. Alle opne ordrar vert gjorde opp i løpet av dei næraste vekene. Nettsidene vert verande ei stund til, slik at de kan hente ut historikk. Noko nedetid må påreknast i juli, fordi vi må omorganisere maskinparken og redusere utgiftene.\n\nFleire har teke kontakt for å kjøpe kundane våre. Det er ikkje aktuelt. I personvernvilkåra våre står det at vi ikkje utleverer informasjon om kundane våre til nokon, med mindre lova krev det. Andre har vore ute etter å kjøpe selskapet med kundane. Det ville vore å omgå vilkåret. Eg har difor bestemt meg for å heller ikkje gjere det, trass i at eg då ville fått att mykje av det eg har investert i Bitmynt. Vi stengjer i staden butikken permanent. Kundeinformasjon vert sletta so snart vi har lov til det.\n\nI staden har vi fått på plass ei heilt frivillig ordning med Bare Bitcoin. Bare Bitcoin er òg ei enkel vekslingsteneste, som i tillegg tilbyr oppbevaring og ein app. Dersom du registrerer deg via lenkja, får du bb+ i 6 månader. Det vil seie at du får gratis handel for opptil 21 000 kroner kvar månad, gratis uttak, litt raskare kundestøtte og meir som vert annonsert snart. Dette er eit veldig godt tilbod! Vi deler ingen personinformasjon med Bare Bitcoin, dei ser berre at du kjem frå denne lenka: https://bb.no/invitert/bitmynt\n\nDet har vore litt av ei reise, men alle reiser har ein ende. No er det på tide for oss å gå vidare til andre ting. Bitcoin lever fint vidare utan Bitmynt. Takk for oss og takk for handelen!\n\n– Sturle Sunde»

If someone asks how much bitcoin they need to retire, the first number I want usually isn't their bitcoin balance.\n\nI want to know what their life costs.\n\nA clean BTC target sounds better because it travels faster. One bitcoin. 6.15 bitcoin. Some round number that feels like a finish line. Those can be useful for motivation, but they aren't enough for a retirement decision because retirement is a coverage problem.\n\nCan your accessible portfolio fund your expenses for as long as you need it to?\n\nThat answer starts with three inputs: annual expenses, liquid investment portfolio value, and time horizon. Expenses tell you what has to be funded. Liquid assets tell you how much usable wealth you already have. Time horizon tells you how long bitcoin has to work before it needs to help pay the bills.\n\nTwo households can have the same net worth and need completely different BTC targets if one has most of the money trapped in home equity, or if one wants to retire now while the other has ten years of runway.\n\nAfter that, you still have to stress-test taxes, account access, withdrawal order, bear markets, and spending flexibility. But at least you're solving the right problem.\n\nRead the full piece: https://www.firebtc.io/p/the-3-inputs-before-anyone-can-answer

‍Enterprise Stablecoin USDGO Surpasses $500 Million in Circulating Supply\n\nThe compliant enterprise stablecoin USDGO has reached a circulating supply of over US$500 million, just four months after its launch. Issued by Anchorage Digital Bank N.A. and distributed by OSL Group, USDGO supports large-value cross-border payments and corporate treasury management under a federally regulated framework.\n\nThe stablecoin previously crossed the US$100 million mark in April 2026. Its growth is driven by integrations with payment providers, infrastructure on the Solana blockchain and Fireblocks, and custody services from Cactus Custody and Amber Group. USDGO is pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and backed by high-quality liquid assets, including JPMorgan's JLTXX, BlackRock's BUIDL, and Goldman Sachs' STBXX.\n\nJason Liu of OSL Group stated that reserve diversification ensures transparency and security for corporate clients. The rise of USDGO reflects the growing collaboration between traditional finance and regulated crypto entities, aiming to become a primary liquidity tool for the digital finance era.\n\nhttps://cryptovka.com/news/enterprise-stablecoin-usdgo-hits-500-million-circulating-supply

‍BlackRock Launches BITA ETF for Double-Digit Bitcoin Yields\n\nBlackRock has introduced the iShares Bitcoin Premium Income ETF (BITA), trading on Nasdaq. This new ETF offers investors direct Bitcoin exposure combined with monthly income through an options overlay strategy, aiming for mid-to-high teens yields.\n\nThe fund splits assets between physical Bitcoin and the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT). Rant.\n\nSomeone's writing proper blockchain history in Korean on the Cardano forum and this is exactly the kind of content that matters more than people realise.\n\nThe framing here is useful. First generation solved trust. Second generation added programmability. Third generation is about making it all actually sustainable. That last bit is where most people's eyes glaze over but it's the whole game.\n\nHere's what I keep coming back to. Bitcoin proved you could have sound money without a central issuer. Ethereum proved you could run code on that foundation. But neither solved the question of how you keep this running for decades without either calcifying into something unchangeable or centralising around whoever has the most resources to maintain it.\n\nCardano's bet is that formal methods, peer review, and on-chain governance aren't academic luxuries. They're load-bearing infrastructure for something that needs to outlast any single team or company. Boring? Maybe. But so is reinforced concrete and we still use it for buildings we expect to stand.\n\nThe generational framing isn't just marketing. It's a genuinely different design philosophy. Whether it pays off is still playing out but the thesis is coherent and the execution is methodical. YMMV but that's how I think about it.\n\nhttps://forum.cardano.org/t/topic/155094\n\nhttps://pool.pm/33502e7de0cc0331534210f16726b7c0c8407ca40e2ab2754dff0bd5/stake\n\n#Cardano #CardanoCommunity

‍Karma3 Labs Shuts Down OpenRank Protocol\n\nKarma3 Labs, the developer of the decentralized reputation framework OpenRank, has announced the cessation of its operations after three and a half years. The protocol will be shut down, and remaining capital will be returned to investors.\n\nOpenRank provided trust scores for over 10 million on-chain users, facilitated over $50 million in incentives, and integrated with more than 50 applications. This is quietly significant. Treasury funds flowing to a VC fund with zero community oversight would be a governance failure. Instead we get a volunteer board seat specifically to represent ADA holders in how that capital gets deployed.\n\nThe cynical take is that a voluntary position has no teeth. Maybe. But the alternative was no seat at all. This is Cardano doing what Cardano does — building accountability structures before the money flows, not after the scandal.\n\nCompare this to how most crypto treasuries operate. Foundation insiders pick the investments, community finds out via Discord screenshot, everyone argues about whether it was a rug or just incompetence. Here we're getting formal representation baked into the legal structure of the fund itself.\n\nIs it perfect? No. Will whoever takes this role have genuine influence? Depends entirely on who applies and how seriously Arouet takes the position. But the fact that this mechanism exists at all is the point. Governance isn't just voting on proposals. It's having your person in the room when decisions get made.\n\nWorth watching who steps up for this.\n\nhttps://forum.cardano.org/t/call-for-applications-voluntary-cardano-community-director/155102\n\nDelegate to BIKES if you want a stake pool that actually reads the governance forum: https://pool.pm/33502e7de0cc0331534210f16726b7c0c8407ca40e2ab2754dff0bd5/stake\n\n#Cardano #CardanoCommunity

QCAP permet la création de défis cryptographiques à difficulté ajustable et publiquement auditables dont la résolution révélerait l'existence d'ordinateurs quantiques capables de casser le problème du logarithme discret sur les courbes elliptiques (Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem, ECDLP).\n\nL'une des particularités de QCAP réside dans son mécanisme d'incitation économique : les défis sont associés à des récompenses en bitcoins, créant ainsi une motivation financière pour qu'un acteur disposant d'une capacité de calcul quantique pertinente tente de les résoudre. Le déplacement des fonds agirait alors comme un signal public indiquant qu'un seuil critique a potentiellement été franchi dans le domaine du calcul quantique.\n\nLe protocole est décentralisé, sécurisé, efficace et vérifiable. Il offre un niveau de difficulté ajustable ainsi qu'une compatibilité native avec Bitcoin. Une implémentation de preuve de concept démontre la faisabilité de QCAP en tant que système d'alerte précoce fondé sur Bitcoin, destiné à détecter l'émergence d'une puissance de calcul quantique susceptible de compromettre les mécanismes cryptographiques actuels. \nhttps://bitcoin.fr/seminaire-de-cryptofinance-quantum-canary-address-generation/

This directive targets exchanges offering USD-denominated wallets without regulatory approval, aiming to enforce financial statutes and control the foreign exchange ecosystem.\n\nThese platforms have been using bank transfers and payment cards, violating the Payment Systems and Services Act, 2019, and the Foreign Exchange Act, 2006. Rant. Everyone obsesses over TPS and TVL metrics while ignoring the thing that actually determines whether a chain survives the next decade. Governance. Who decides what changes. How disputes get resolved. Whether the protocol can evolve without forking into oblivion or ossifying into irrelevance.\n\nThis Korean forum piece frames it well. Technology you can build. Getting humans to collectively operate it without tearing each other apart is the actual hard problem. Blockchain governance is not a code problem. It is a coordination problem wrapped in game theory wrapped in centuries of failed political experiments.\n\nWhat strikes me about Cardano's approach with CIP-1694 and the constitutional convention is that it treats governance as infrastructure, not an afterthought. Most chains either pretend governance does not exist, hand it to a foundation that becomes a shadow dictatorship, or bolt on token voting that just recreates plutocracy with extra steps.\n\nThe meta-governance question this piece raises matters more than people realize. Who governs the governors. How do you change the rules for changing rules. Get this wrong and your shiny decentralized protocol becomes a cartel with better PR.\n\nStill early days. Voltaire is messy. DReps are learning. But at least there is a framework being stress-tested in public rather than decisions happening in Signal groups.\n\nhttps://forum.cardano.org/t/topic/155112\n\nYMMV but I think governance is the sleeper differentiator for the next cycle. O Próximo Problema do Milênio: Uma Análise Bayesiana\n\nhttps://web.archive.org/web/20260616023355/https://dn1.cess.network/426053737.pdf\n\nEste documento apresenta um estudo técnico que utiliza a probabilidade bayesiana para estimar qual dos Problemas do Milênio será o próximo a ser solucionado. O autor fundamenta sua análise combinando crenças racionais iniciais com evidências matemáticas recentes, como avanços em resultados parciais e a existência de barreiras técnicas. A Conjectura de Birch e Swinnerton-Dyer emerge como a favorita com 51,6% de probabilidade, seguida pelas equações de Navier-Stokes com 31,2%. Em contrapartida, problemas como P versus NP e a Hipótese de Riemann apresentam chances reduzidas devido à complexidade extrema e ao histórico de tentativas frustradas. O texto conclui que, embora a matemática seja imprevisível, esse modelo oferece uma forma rigorosa e sistemática de quantificar o progresso científico atual. \n\n \n\n

Not glamorous, not optimised for maximum yield extraction, but it's honest stake in the network.\n\nThe thing about Cardano's stake pool design is it actually wants pools like this to exist. The k parameter, the a0 factor — it's all built to spread stake across many operators rather than concentrating in a handful of mega pools. Whether that's working as intended is another conversation, but the architecture at least tries.\n\nAnyway. We keep the node running, the epochs keep ticking. Next one might hit, might not. YMMV as always.\n\nhttps://pool.pm/33502e7de0cc0331534210f16726b7c0c8407ca40e2ab2754dff0bd5/stake\n\n#CardanoStaking

VARA Дубая ужесточает контроль: ежеквартальная оценка рисков для криптофирм\n\nУправление по регулированию виртуальных активов Дубая (VARA) обязало криптокомпании перейти на динамические модели оценки рисков. Новые требования предусматривают анализ количественных бизнес-данных в режиме реального времени и отказ от статичных методов мониторинга.\n\nСогласно новым правилам, поставщики услуг в сфере виртуальных активов (VASP) должны проводить комплексную переоценку рисков не реже одного раза в квартал. Внеплановые корректировки стратегии риск-менеджмента требуются при внедрении новых продуктов или существенных изменениях в структуре компании.\n\nVARA также уделяет внимание рискам, связанным с использованием искусственного интеллекта (AI) и конфиденциальных монет, а также с юрисдикциями из «черных» и «серых» списков FATF. Ожидается, что переход на автоматизированные системы оценки повысит эффективность борьбы с финансовыми преступлениями.\n\nhttps://cryptovka.ru/news/vara-dubaya-uzhestochaet-kontrol-ezhekvartalnaya-ocenka-riskov-dlya-kriptofirm
